title: Direct Connect vs VPN vs internet
scenario: Orrin Genomics' sequencing lab pushes about 10 TB of run data to AWS every night inside a 6-hour window, so the transfer must sustain roughly 4 Gbps for analysis to start at 06:00. A two-week trial over the public internet showed throughput falling to 1.5 Gbps at busy times, and the transfer tool aborts if the rate stays below 3 Gbps for 5 minutes. The data-protection policy requires encryption in transit for all lab data, the research director needs a pilot to start within five days, and the network provider quotes several weeks for any new physical circuit. The lab has budget for one physical circuit only; if it fails, the nightly transfer must still complete within 36 hours (a one-night backlog is acceptable) and that day's analysis may be skipped, because the 3 Gbps abort rule applies only to normal nightly runs. The pilot may move a 1 TB subset at whatever rate it reaches.
constraints: Do not claim live AWS experience
The research director needs a pilot flowing within five days, before any new physical circuit can be delivered
The data-protection officer requires encryption in transit for all lab data on every path
Finance funds one physical circuit only, so resilience cannot come from a second circuit; the transfer takes up to 36 hours (a one-night backlog is acceptable) while that circuit is down
requiredArtifact: Architecture decision record + diagram notes + cost assumptions

rubric.label: Why live lab was unsuitable documented
Steady-state nightly path sustains more than 4 Gbps, and the design shows why the 1.5 Gbps internet dips do not occur on it
Pilot within five days, encryption in transit on every path, and a working path while the circuit is down (transfer within 36 hours) are each met and each states the rate that path can sustain

constraint_reason: Service unavailable or not disposable in a personal same-day lab
